audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows contradict their own whys[]. The file gives Level 1 to Skill (its why says 'He out-trades your single ability at Level 1'), Levels 2 and 3 to Pantheon (whys say you complete W-root into Q and his spear 'can't out-damage your sustain'), Levels 4-5 to Skill (why says you 'grind out repeat favorable trades'), and first item and 2+ items to Pantheon (whys say he 'has no scaling answer' and 'zero item scaling'). The lane is also labelled TRICKY at 7.5/10 against a 59.77% win rate.
audit.why: Pantheon owns Level 1 outright — Comet Spear plus a point-and-click Shield Vault stun against one Maokai ability. From Level 2 Twisted Advance into Bramble Smash reverses it, and Pantheon has no item scaling to answer Maokai's resists and sustain later. Only Level 6 is genuinely even: Grand Starfall is a 180s roam tool and Nature's Grasp is gank setup; neither decides a duel.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Pantheon / Maokai / Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Maokai / Maokai in both layers (the packet chart), difficulty relabelled EVEN at 5/10.

audit.why: Four spikes present, and unusually they are correctly sequenced as Lvl 1 (his), Lvl 2-3 (yours), Lvl 6 (neither), 1st item (yours). That ordering is what the chart should have matched all along.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions are absent. First: nothing states that Sap Magic's cooldown drops each time Maokai is struck by an enemy spell, so Pantheon's poke actively funds Maokai's healing. Second: Aegis Assault is a channel that is invulnerable only from the front — nothing in the file says either that it is interruptible or that it is directional. dosFull[2] and dontsFull[1] both carry descriptions unrelated to their own titles.
audit.why: Riot's Sap Magic text: 'Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced.' Pantheon's whole lane plan is chip, and chip is self-defeating into that passive — the mirror audit on pantheon reached the same conclusion. Aegis Assault carries both the 'channel: interruptible — any CC cancels it' and 'shield' flags with Riot's text specifying invulnerability 'from the front', so Maokai's W root or Q knockback cancels it and a flank ignores it entirely. On a 22s rank-1 cooldown, cancelling it is the single highest-value button press in the matchup.
audit.corrected: phases[3].why now states the Sap Magic refresh; dosFull[2].d states the channel interrupt; dontsFull[1].d states the frontal-only blocking.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no Pantheon ability is ever named except Shield Vault, and Shield Vault is never given a cooldown.
audit.why: Shield Vault is 13/12/11/10/9s and Grand Starfall is 180/165/150s. The first number tells you how long your window is after he uses his stun; the second tells you a used ultimate is off the map for three minutes.
audit.corrected: Comet Spear, Shield Vault, Aegis Assault and Grand Starfall now named with cooldowns across phases[0], phases[2], phases[4], dosFull[0] and dontsFull[1].

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Pantheon contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Comet Spear poke plus a point-click Shield Vault stun beat your one ability before your combo exists — concede the level.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Pantheon's Shield Vault is down.
edits.after: W-root into Q-Bramble lands and Sap Magic heals it back — his spear cannot out-damage your sustain from Level 2 on.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Pantheon must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Saplings zone his poke and you repeat W-into-Q faster than Shield Vault, an 11s cooldown at rank 3, comes back.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Shield Vault's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Every spell he lands on you shortens Sap Magic's cooldown, so his poke funds your heal — grind repeat trades all through 4-5.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Pantheon's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grand Starfall is a roam tool on a 180s cooldown and Nature's Grasp is gank setup — neither swings the 1v1, so 6 is even.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Shield Vault's cooldown.
edits.after: Your first sustain item makes resists and Sap Magic eat his spear; he has no scaling.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Pantheon carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Pantheon has zero item scaling — your durability and healing out-last him outright while he has nothing left to add.

edits.before: His all-in start. Root/peel it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Shield Vault is his all-in start, 13s at rank 1. Root it or trade after.

edits.before: Pantheon wastes Shield Vault (Stun) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Aegis Assault is a channel — your W root or Q knockback cancels it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Aegis Assault only blocks the front — flank it or Q him out of it.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Shield Vault and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. You lose Level 1, then win every stage after it once W-Q and Sap Magic come online.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Pantheon carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 5/10, Pantheon carry threat 7/10.

notes: Largest correction in this slice. A 59.77% matchup was rendered as TRICKY 7.5/10 with six of seven chart rows inverted against the file's own prose. Two genuine mechanical gaps closed, both confirmed by the mirror audit: Pantheon's chip refreshes Sap Magic (his lane plan feeds your passive), and Aegis Assault is an interruptible channel that only blocks damage from the front — Maokai's W root or Q knockback cancels a 22s ability outright. dontsFull[1] is still titled 'Sit low for his W execute'; Shield Vault has no execute component in Riot's text, but the title is under the applier's 25-character floor so I left it — flagging it for a title pass.
